title: Refine the epic
do: In Home, type /, pick Iterate on something, type: No-show fees moved up to end of October. Help me refine BOK-300 so Rebecca's team can start at sprint planning on Wednesday. Round one: Cut it on Per sitting, Keep it on the other two, skip Anything else. Round two: keep all three.
offScript: That is outside what this demo can show. The six things it can do are listed in Settings, under Demo.

text: The first release of no-show fees, as three stories before sprint planning on 2026-07-22 ([[meetings/2026-07-13-1-1-rebecca]]). Deciding: what is in the first release ([[tickets/jira/BOK-300]]). Out of scope: a date, and anything the Payments team owns ([[tickets/jira/PAY-190]] is done, deposits are not ours). Done looks like: three stories with three checks each, so Rebecca's team can start on Wednesday.
Three ideas first. Keep or cut each one.

questions.question: In the notes from the Brasserie Lund review on 2026-06-02, one idea was to let a restaurant set a different fee for lunch and dinner ([[meetings/2026-06-02-brasserie-lund-review]]). Is it in scope for October?
questions.body:
The case: Lena asked for it in June and again yesterday, and it is still an open question on the research page ([[research/no-show-fees]]). A restaurant that serves lunch and dinner would set a lower fee at lunch.

The cost: two amounts per restaurant, on the settings page, on the booking page and on the receipt. The working notes say one fee per restaurant in the first release ([[notes/fee-rules]]). Every extra amount is a story the team has to estimate before October.

options.label: Keep it
options.description: A fourth story for a lunch fee and a dinner fee. October gets tighter.

options.label: Cut it
options.description: One fee per restaurant. The lunch and dinner idea stays open on the research page for a later release.

questions.question: Charge the fee on online and Google bookings only, so a booking a member of staff takes by phone gets no fee. Keep that for the first release?
questions.body:
The case: a guest who books by phone never saw the notice, so there is nothing to charge. The working notes already say so ([[notes/fee-rules]]), and the epic says the same ([[tickets/jira/BOK-300]]).

The cost: a restaurant that takes many bookings by phone gets fees on part of its list, and the booking list has to show which bookings carry a fee.

options.label: Keep it
options.description: The stories say online and Google bookings only, in plain words.

options.label: Cut it
options.description: Then the stories need a way for staff to take a card over the phone, which is a story nobody has written.

questions.question: Run an A/B test on the wording of the fee notice on the booking page, on a few restaurants, before every restaurant gets it?
questions.body:
The case: the working notes flag that the wording of the notice may change how many guests finish the booking ([[notes/fee-rules]]). Two wordings on a few restaurants first means Brasserie Lund's 40 restaurants get the one that costs fewer bookings ([[customers/brasserie-lund]]).

The cost: a third story, with a switch per restaurant and a report. It is work before October, and it has to run before the fee goes to every restaurant.

options.label: Keep it
options.description: One story: two wordings, a few restaurants, a report of completed bookings per wording.

options.label: Cut it
options.description: One wording for everyone, and we find out in December whether it cost bookings.

questions.question: What is missing, what should merge, what did I get wrong?

text: One fee per restaurant: the lunch and dinner fee is cut. The stories cover online and Google bookings only, and the notice wording gets a test.
Three stories, three checks each. Keep or cut.

questions.question: Card on file at booking.
questions.body:
- The guest enters a card on the booking page when the restaurant has fees on.
- The card is stored through PAY-190 and never in the bookings service.
- The confirmation says a fee applies and how much.

questions.question: Charge the fee after a no-show.
questions.body:
- The restaurant marks the booking as a no-show from the booking list.
- The charge goes through the next morning, not on the spot.
- The guest gets a receipt by text.

questions.question: Fee notice wording test.
questions.body:
- Two wordings of the notice.
- A restaurant gets one or the other.
- The report shows completed bookings per wording.

questions.question: Anything to change before they become tickets?

turns.text: Three ticket cards wait under BOK-300, one per story, in the team's shape: the label, Brasserie Lund in the first line, three checks. The reasoning stays in this session.

input.title: Card on file at booking
input.body:
Brasserie Lund needs this before their Christmas bookings open on 1 November: a card on file at booking, so a no-show can be charged.

Part of BOK-300 (no-show fees), first release. One fee per restaurant. Online and Google bookings only; a booking a member of staff takes by phone gets no fee. Card storage through PAY-190, which is done.

Acceptance:
- [ ] The guest enters a card on the booking page when the restaurant has fees on.
- [ ] The card is stored through PAY-190 and never in the bookings service.
- [ ] The confirmation says a fee applies and how much.

Source: story round in Qale, 2026-07-17
input.rationale: First of the three stories you kept. The other two need a card on file before they can charge anything.

input.title: Charge the fee after a no-show
input.body:
Brasserie Lund lost about one table a night per restaurant to no-shows last December: this is the charge that makes the card on file worth taking.

Part of BOK-300 (no-show fees), first release. The restaurant decides from the booking list; the charge runs the next morning, so a manager can undo a mistake the same evening. Uses the token PAY-190 stores.

Acceptance:
- [ ] The restaurant marks the booking as a no-show from the booking list.
- [ ] The charge goes through the next morning, not on the spot.
- [ ] The guest gets a receipt by text.

Source: story round in Qale, 2026-07-17
input.rationale: Second of the three stories you kept. Charged the morning after, as the working notes say.

input.title: Fee notice wording test
input.body:
Brasserie Lund's 40 restaurants get the fee first, so the notice wording gets a test on a few restaurants before every restaurant sees it.

Part of BOK-300 (no-show fees), first release. Two wordings of the notice on the booking page, a switch per restaurant, and a report, so we know before December whether the notice costs bookings.

Acceptance:
- [ ] Two wordings of the notice.
- [ ] A restaurant gets one or the other.
- [ ] The report shows completed bookings per wording.

Source: story round in Qale, 2026-07-17
input.rationale: Third of the three stories you kept: the test you said yes to in round one.

input.append: Done 2026-07-17: three stories drafted under [[tickets/jira/BOK-300]] (card on file at booking, charge the fee after a no-show, fee notice wording test), three checks each, ahead of sprint planning on 2026-07-22. The lunch and dinner fee is cut from the first release. The rounds and the reasoning are in the session that drafted them.
input.rationale: The stories are drafted, three of them with three checks each, before the 2026-07-21 due date, so the commitment from the 1:1 is met.
